info.title: ArcPanel REST API v2
info.description:
Resource API of an ArcPanel server, served by the panel at `/api/v2/` (port 8083 by default). Every call acts as the owner of the access key, with the role and the reach that user has in the panel: objects outside its reach answer `404`, refused actions `403`.

**Authentication.** `Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_KEY_ID:SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, an access key of the panel (Account → Access keys). The API must be on (`API_SYSTEM` 1 for the administrator's keys, 2 for every key) and accept the client's address (`API_ALLOWED_IP`). A key with permission sets may only run their commands: `v2-read` allows the read endpoints, `v2-write` every endpoint. Both sets are refused by API v1. `GET /me` describes the key.

**Dry run.** Every write accepts `?dry_run=1`: the request is validated, authorized and checked against the permission sets, and the answer lists the commands it would run, without running any.

**Errors.** Every error answers `{"error": {"code": "E_…", "message": "…"}}`; `code` is one of `ErrorCode`. Validation errors add `fields`, refused permission sets add `commands`, a failed step of a change adds `step` and the steps that ran before it (`applied`), which stay applied.

**Headers.** Every answer carries `ArcPanel-Version` and `X-Request-Id` (the client's own value, or a new one). `429` carries `Retry-After`; `201` and `202` carry `Location`. Each key may make 60 requests a minute; ten failed authentications a minute block the client's address for a minute.

**Compatibility.** Within v2 the document only grows: new operations, new optional fields, new enum values. Clients should ignore unknown fields.

The access key of the request: its owner and role, its permission
sets and the commands they allow (`*` when unrestricted), and the
versions of the panel and of the API. Clients use it to check a
profile (E34 spec D12).

Every package but `system` for an administrator, the packages a
reseller may assign for a reseller.

Fields left out take the values of the add form of the panel. A
reseller's package is stored as RESELLER_NAME and may not exceed the
reseller's own limits; the `reseller` settings are an administrator's.
A repeated call answers 409 `E_EXISTS`.

ApiRole.description: Role of a user in API v2 answers and requests.
ApiRole.title: ApiRole

command.description: The v-* command of the step.

args.description: Arguments of the command; secrets are masked.

fields.description: E_VALIDATION: the messages of each invalid field.

commands.description: E_FORBIDDEN by a permission set: the commands the key may not run.

step.description: The step of a change that failed.

applied.description: The steps that ran before the failed one; they stay applied.

ErrorCode.description: Error names of the command exit codes (func/main.sh) and of the API layer.

user.description: the owner of the key; every call acts as this user

read_only.description: whether the user may only read (no write endpoint answers)

commands.description: the commands the key may run, `*` when unrestricted

name.description: the name in paths; a reseller's own packages are stored as RESELLER_NAME

label.description: the name as its owner sees it

owner.description: the reseller that created the package; null for the administrator's

rate_limit.description: outgoing mails an hour per account

resources.description: cgroup limits, applied when the server has RESOURCES_LIMIT='yes' (values such as 50%, 100ms, 512M)

reseller.description: What a reseller on this package may do (E11)

users.description: customers a reseller on this package may have

packages.description: packages it may assign, `*` for every visible one

visible.description: whether resellers may assign this package

allowed.description: `lts`, `*` or a list of major versions

created_at.description: creation time in the server's time zone, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS

command.description: The v-* command of the step.

StorePackageRequest.title: StorePackageRequest

StoreUserRequest.description:
POST /users: the account of the create wizard (E11 spec §7.3). Role,
owner and login_disabled are an administrator's choices; for a reseller
the new user is always its own customer.

username.description: The login name: 2 to 30 of a-z, 0-9, dot, dash and underscore.

password.description: At least 8 characters with a lower-case and an upper-case letter and a digit.

package.description: A package the caller may assign (see GET /packages).

language.description: A language of the server; the server language when left out.

owner.description: Administrators only: the administrator or a reseller that owns a new user.

StoreUserRequest.title: StoreUserRequest

UpdatePackageRequest.title: UpdatePackageRequest

UpdateUserRequest.title: UpdateUserRequest

owner.description: the reseller or administrator that owns the user; null for administrators

created_at.description: creation time in the server's time zone, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS

package.description: A package the caller may assign (see GET /packages).

password.description: At least 8 characters with a lower-case and an upper-case letter and a digit.

Unauthenticated.description: The access key is missing, unknown or wrong (`E_UNAUTHENTICATED`).

Forbidden.description: The API is off for this key (`E_API_DISABLED`), the role or a permission set refuses the call (`E_FORBIDDEN`), or the owner is suspended (`E_SUSPENDED`).

NotFound.description: No such object in the scope of the key (`E_NOTEXIST`).

Conflict.description: The object exists or is in use (`E_EXISTS`, `E_INUSE`).

ValidationFailed.description: The request is invalid (`E_VALIDATION` with `fields`, or a command refused an argument).

TooManyRequests.description: Too many requests (`E_RATE_LIMIT`, or a package limit `E_LIMIT`); `Retry-After` names the seconds to wait.

ServerError.description: A command failed on the server.

Unavailable.description: The service is disabled or the server is too busy (`E_DISABLED`, `E_LA`).

accessKey.description: An access key of the panel and its secret, joined by a colon.

RequestId.description: The id of the request: the client's X-Request-Id, or a new one.

RetryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before the next request.

Location.description: URL of the resource (201) or of the resource to poll (202).
